newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb higher while feeder cattle were called 0.100 to 0.200 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Expectations packers will have to pay at least another $1 per cwt for cash cattle encouraged ideas of carryover support in live cattle futures. Boxed beef values rose sharply on Monday and this should keep packer demand strong for cash cattle, analysts said.
Boxed beef values rose $1.06 to 1.56 per cwt Monday.
They also cited the South Korean beef tender results which showed they are purchasing 2,483 tonnes of U.S. chuck roll for late August arrival.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to remain under pressure following further strength in corn futures. Higher corn futures overnight and higher indications for Tuesday morning's opening should weigh on feeders and offset the recent strength in cash feeders, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.44 at $82.56 per cwt, the highest level since March 4, 1994.
